results.text: Beta 2-adrenergic pathway combats Alzheimer's disease: Restoring cognition and synaptic integrity. Alzheimer's disease is typified by amyloid-beta oligomer-mediated synaptic disruption, neuroinflammation, and mitochondrial loss of function, culminating in cognitive decline. Recent evidence points toward the β2- adrenergic receptor as a target through its regulation of synaptic plasticity, neuroinflammation, and epigenetic control. Chronically elevated neurohumoral drive, and particularly elevated adrenergic tone leading to β-adrenergic receptor (β-AR) overstimulation in cardiac myocytes, is a key mechanism involved in the progression of heart failure. β1-AR (β1-adrenergic receptor) and β2-ARs (β2-adrenergic receptor) are the 2 major subtypes of β-ARs present in the human heart; however, they elicit different or even opposite effects on cardiac function
